design_condition: The longitudinal volume is placed in the narrow bend of the street, extending the existing gymnasium and kindergarten into a terraced complex while organizing a continuous inner axis and differentiated outdoor spaces on the sloping site.

positive.statement: The volumetric addition, terracing and internal access axis clearly allocate the open spaces.
The actual units are elaborate, find synergies, offer different types of play and are well lit without wasting circulation space.
The floor plans are tidy, clearly structured and well and functionally organized.
The base floor reacts adequately to the falling street and supports the three units.
The economical footprint is comparatively efficient.

negative.statement: Relieving the access from through traffic is not realistic, making the access problematic.
The opposing small buildings create a difficult spatial situation, and the northern buildings are too close to the linden tree.
The design of the southern tip is not convincing and unnecessarily restricts the outdoor space.
The allocation of the outdoor areas is comparatively rigid and does not allow smooth transitions.
The inner axis merges with care circulation areas and makes delivery to the units more difficult.
A homely, child-friendly atmosphere is not achieved, and the type remains too closely related to the schoolhouse.
The groups are difficult to manage because they are spread over two floors.
The additive principle cannot convincingly resolve the beginning and the end of the building.
The building cannot be developed into the postulated sculpture.
The facades remain trapped at the level of unity and only partially break through the isolation.
